preamble: Palatalization and affrication of the aspirated alveolar stop [tʰ] to the aspirated alveolo-palatal affricate [tɕʰ] before /i/ and /j/. It is the aspirated half of the Korean t-palatalization, in which Middle Korean ㄷ /t/ and ㅌ /tʰ/ before /i/ or /j/ became ㅈ and ㅊ. The Pyongan and Yukjin dialects did not undergo the change and still read many of these syllables with ㅌ.

examples.from: Middle Korean 고티〮다〮 kwòthítá 'to straighten, to fix' (1447)
Middle Korean 톄〮 thyéy, Sino-Korean reading of 體 'body'
examples.note: Here the trigger is the palatal glide /j/; Early Modern Korean and the Pyongan and Yukjin dialects keep 톄 or 테.
